The joint auditor instead requires each participating member material to equal frame.material; otherwise it adds invalid_timber_joint_contact even when the other joint checks would pass. The public audit path invokes that timber audit. The same historical 6533 audit source was independently displayed at the relevant gate, while the current builder initializes generated members uniformly from its frame material.

Other geometric/contact/material conditions still apply independently.

findings_and_reconciliations.trace: StoreyIndex accepts native usize and checks u16 capacity at serialization; from_elevation rounds first, rejects nonfinite, negative rounded ordinals and values above u16, then casts. A small negative elevation rounding to signed zero is consistent with the documented rounded-station policy; a valid index still is not proof of membership in a specific building. The two building model blobs match 6533 and 95e exactly, with distinct personal displays. In rust-quality, compared old/current windows show added, removed and moved scope records and the unchanged top-level numeric limits; the checker interprets scope kinds and checks stale path/item references. thirteen_lens_perspectives.bounded_assessment: Storey wire capacity and elevation conversion are explicit, while timber participant defaults and graph/material admission need actual caller policy.
Individual member IDs, nodes, endpoints and material do not alone guarantee joint graph coherence; a joint auditor currently compares each material to assembly default.
Preserve documented rounded station semantics, separate native and wire ordinal ranges, current quality policy scopes and independent structural checks while investigating potential mixed materials.
Transparent typed IDs and derived serde serve distinct identities; blindly deriving StoreyIndex wire serialization would lose checked narrowing semantics.
Timber member role, phase and material and explicitly empty or populated participant state represent distinct concepts; no blanket enum replacement follows.
StoreyIndex is a canonical ordinal but membership is a separate building-specific contract; timber role/material/IDs already have named owners.
Checked float-to-ordinal conversion rejects overflow; round-to-zero of small negatives is intentional under the stated station policy, not necessarily below-ground failure.
Quality limits and timber dimensions encode distinct policy/physical units; acceptance thresholds and scanner scope exemptions must be examined at their owning source.
Quality config paths/items/reasons and audit issue codes are policy/native diagnostic representations; scope names are not product validation, and no string-dispatch finding is established here.
Initial timber builder assigns frame material to members while audit requires equality; actual later repair/addition producers and final building consumer must be traced.
Member-local material and frame default have a source-documented role distinction; uniform joint audit potentially overrides member-local authority under mixed-material conditions.
Wire ordinal capacity, native vector index, structural identity, material and geographic direction have different semantic boundaries; no primitive-based universal merge.
Central reconciliation must decide the member-local structural policy and checker exception owner; historical supplier or matched object identity is not repair ownership.
